title: Man shot, killed by Peel Police described as 'violent drug dealer'
article: A Brampton man shot and killed by Peel Regional Police during a routine traffic stop Wednesday night was once described by Vancouver Police as a well-known "street-level enforcer with a long history of violence, drug trafficking and drug possession."
Jermaine Carby, 33, was shot dead by a Peel Police officer after the Black Jetta he was in was pulled over by a uniformed patrol officer on Queen St., near Kennedy Rd., just after 10 p.m.
The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) is investigating to determine whether the shooting was justified.
The SIU has designated one subject officer and five witness officers.
Police said it was a traffic stop, but had no information about the reason for the stop.
The officer radioed for a backup unit "a short time later", but there were no indications anything was wrong, according to Peel Const. Thomas Ruttan.
The officer later pushed his emergency button indicating he needs help immediately, Ruttan said.
A short time after that, shots were fired and an occupant of the Jetta who had gotten out of the car, was fatally wounded.
Eyewitness Richard Appleby saw the incident unfold and told reporters Carby was slowly walking towards police with his arms stretched out seconds before he was shot.
"I heard the police officer say 'drop the knife' a couple of times and something to effect of 'don't make us shoot you," Appleby said. "Like, 'we don't want to shoot you, drop the knife.'"
Appleby said he heard several shots but did not see a knife.
Other witnesses told reporters more than one shot was fired - between three and five have been reported by passersby - and one said the dead man had a knife.
The SIU has not released any details on what happened or how many shots were fired.
No police officers were injured in the incident.
Vancouver police said in 2011 Carby had had 110 interactions with police, with a criminal record dating back to 2000 in Toronto.

He has been charged 28 times in the past, Vancouver Police said. In summer 2011, he was charged with manslaughter in connection with a fatal stabbing in Vancouver's Oppenheimer Park and two counts of assault involving two women.
Court documents do show that Carby was found guilty of uttering threats in 2012 and possession for the purpose of trafficking in 2008 and 2009.
Mourners who gathered at the scene of the shooting Thursday, where a makeshift memorial of flowers had been set up, say Carby was a good man who helps out his friends and family members.
Lorna Robinson, Carby's mother, said people should not believe reports from British Columbia that her son was an infamous drug enforcer.
"I don't know exactly what was going on," she said of Wednesday's shooting. "I want to see justice served. I want to see justice done."
